subject: Fluxly onboarding: benchmark ramp coordination
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@fluxly.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@fluxly.com, Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@fluxly.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fluxly onboarding: benchmark ramp coordination

Hi Ben / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Fluxly is ready to start the performance verification window before we flip traffic in Q4. We want to validate that Redwood meets our production latency and throughput expectations using our realistic request mix. High-level asks: 

- Can Redwood commit to a 99th percentile latency of < 250ms for the default conversational model at our steady-state throughput target (25 req/s)?
- We’ll run two stress windows: a capacity ramp (25 -> 200 req/s over 90 minutes) and an endurance soak (48 hours at 80 req/s).
- Need clear success criteria and the artifacts you’ll share (logs, tail-latency histograms, token counts).

We have a short maintenance window on 2026-11-09 for the ramp; can you confirm availability and what you need from our side (test keys, sample prompt set, data redaction guidance)?

Also copying Procurement to start the SOW/PO conversation in parallel.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
CTO, Fluxly Commerce

Daniel — thanks for the clear outline. Monica and I sketched a pragmatic verification plan and I’ve attached the load plan + KPI matrix. Summary: 

- Target SLOs we’ll validate: 99p latency < 250ms, median < 90ms at 25 req/s steady-state; tail-latency heatmaps for the ramp and soak.
- Ramp window target: 2026-11-09 02:00-05:00 UTC (Fluxly confirmed?), incremental checkpoints at 25/50/100/150/200 req/s. Each step runs 10 minutes with 5-minute stabilization.
- Soak window: starting 2026-11-16 00:00 UTC for 48 hours at 80 req/s with telemetry sampling every 5 minutes.
- Artifacts we’ll provide: per-route latency CSVs, aggregated p50/p95/p99 dashboards, token consumption by prompt class, and a condensed runbook with failure-mode notes.

What we need from Fluxly:
- A list of 10 representative prompt templates and a 5000-line test payload file (redacted) by 2026-11-04.
- Confirmation of any special model variants (e.g., quantized, longer context) you want in the run.
- A test API key for the dedicated onboarding cluster and an IP allowlist if you want a VPC-restricted run.

I’ve also included a short pre-run checklist for SREs in the attachment. If that timing works we’ll lock the runbook and loop in Karthik (engineering) for test orchestration.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0183

Thanks — adding details from the CS/implementation side.

Karthik and I will run the orchestrated ramp; here are the acceptance gates we’ll use (explicit, please):

1) Steady-state gate (25 req/s) — pass if p99 < 250ms AND error rate < 0.5% for 15 minutes after warm-up.
2) Ramp-step gate (each increment) — pass if p99 does not increase by > 2x from previous step and error rate stays < 1.5%. Any step that fails will trigger an immediate rollback to last known-good step and a 20-minute investigation pause.
3) Soak gate — pass if no incident-classifier alerts (saturation/memory-leak indicators) and p99 stability within 20% of steady-state for the majority of samples across 48 hours.

Operational notes:
- Please provide a contact in your SRE team who can approve escalation (pager/Slack) during the window.
- We’ll publish a short incident playbook for any observed regressions (attached).
- For evidence sharing we’ll create a read-only Drive folder and deliver a final runbook + artifacts package within 48 hours after the runs.

Daniel — quick question: do you require us to run with payload deduplication disabled? That affects cache hit behavior and flat throughput. If so, note that pass/fail thresholds may shift and we should capture that in the KPI matrix.

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com | +1 650-555-1222
